About a month ago I submitted a post titled A little late to the party... I was excited that I finally had a small area to garden and wanted to share.

I have spent the last 5-6 weeks working on it, and I have some pictures to share. Here is a picture of the first week. The left shows the original space, and the right shows after I added my first few bags of compost and soil.

Buying individual bags wasn't going to cut it, and the "soil" already there is actually black fabric mulch covering about 6 inches of now dead vines and swarms of fire ants (I found out the hard way). An acquaintance of mine generously agreed to pick up 1.5 cubic yards of garden soil in his truck bed and deliver it, and I bought a few plants while waiting for my seeds to germinate. Those pictures are here

I now have 4 types of basil, 12 ocra plants, a few different types of tomatoes, lemon grass, oregano, fennel, tarragon, sage, Laos pumpkins, albino pumpkins, Chinese noodle beans, 4 types of hot peppers, marigolds, nasturtiums, and 6 butternut squash. Here is a picture of what the garden looks like as of a few days ago.

It is so hot here, the only plants doing well are the basil and the ocra. I am hoping that once it cools off my plants will have some relief and really take off.

I ordered seeds for kale, chard, spinach, and two types of beets to plant in the area of the garden that is still empty, but only once it cools down this fall.

I also ordered a syringe of King Stropharia spawn (for wine cap mushrooms), which supposedly grow really well in wood chips. The "garden soil" I purchased has quite of a few wood chips mixed in, so I am going to attempt to inoculate it with the wine cap mushroom spawn now while it is warm, and keep my fingers crossed that as it cools down I might get a flush before Christmas.

There are buds on the ocra, peppers, and tomatoes. I have already been using my herbs almost every day. Sometime in October I'll post another update with pictures of my harvest, and hopefully some kale, chard and beet seedlings. I was lucky enough to catch a small piece on WWNO (NPR New Orleans) about growing seasons in Southern Louisiana, and its possible to still be harvesting tomatoes in December. I hope I will be!
